newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy August PPI seen rising 0.1 pct m/m.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy August PPI seen rising 0.1 pct m/m.

text.p: The current weakness of Italy's economic cycle makes it virtually impossible to see any price pressure at the producer and wholesale level, a Reuter poll of analysts showed.
Analysts showed producer prices rising 0.1 percent in August on a monthly basis and by just 0.05 percent yearly.

"The weakness of the productive cycle is weighing negatively on prices. The lack of demand makes it very difficult to find pressure on prices at the producer or wholesale stage," Lucia Trevisan, economist at Caboto, said.
August PPI and WPI data are due out on Friday.
In July, producer prices fell by 0.2 percent monthly and rose 0.2 percent yearly. In August 1995, PPI rose 0.2 percent monthly and 9.0 percent on a yearly basis.
Analysts see Italian wholesale prices in August rising 0.35 percent on a monthly basis and 2.55 percent on a yearly basis.
In July 1996, wholesale prices fell 0.4 percent month on month and rose 2.6 percent year on year. In August 1995, the WPI rose 0.4 percent monthly and 10.8 percent yearly.
But analysts said there could be some impact, especially on wholesale prices, from the effects of recent price increases in petrol products.
"Proof of this could be seen by possibly higher than expected prices, especially WPI," Deutsche Bank in Milan said in a note.
